rationale: Registered the successor execution that closes the open gap on the client-change channel: the harness adds a client_change_on_reconstruction case where a three-voter cluster is collapsed to one voter, snapshotted and made three voters again, then only the former leader is restarted, a fresh empty instance joins it, a client AddVoter is issued to that leader, and the two demoted peers are finally brought back. Construction-time local feedback: with the flag enabled the change committed (leader configuration two voters, the new member not in the replaced three-voter configuration, both demoted peers ending with no vote and both adopting the new configuration); with the flag disabled the leader could not be elected with the others down, the change failed with "node is not the leader" and the demoted peers kept their votes.

scope.description: Whether a client membership change issued to a node whose configuration is the reconstructed one commits with support that is not a majority of the configuration it replaces, and whether the peers it demotes adopt it. Nineteen in-process cases: the seventeen previously exercised restart shapes plus a client_change_on_reconstruction case run with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and disabled. In that case a three-voter cluster is collapsed to one voter, snapshotted, made three voters again, every instance is stopped, and only the former leader is restarted together with a fresh empty fourth instance; a client AddVoter for that instance is issued with prevIndex 0, and the two demoted peers are then restarted with the flag disabled.
assumptions: Real raft instances in one process over the in-memory transports and the in-memory commit-tracking log store from the captured package; the fresh instance has its own empty log, stable and snapshot stores and is connected to the restarted leader in both directions, and the returning peers are reconnected likewise.
The two peers of the committed configuration are deliberately kept down while the change is issued, so the leader cannot reach them and any commit must rest on itself and the fresh instance.
The client change is the package's own AddVoter with prevIndex 0, as the package's AddPeer and RemovePeer helpers also use.

The change wait is 400 ms and the observation of the returning peers a further 400 ms; the returning peers are restarted with RestoreCommittedLogs disabled so their own configuration comes from their logs.
excluded: Disk-backed stores, real networks, membership changes with a nonzero prevIndex, concurrent client changes, and any claim about leadership among disjoint configurations after a partition.

experiment.prefix: The new case builds a three-peer cluster with MakeClusterCustom(MakeClusterOpts{Peers: 3, Bootstrap: true, CommitTrackingLogs: true, Conf: inmemConfig with TrailingLogs 10 and RestoreCommittedLogs set per case}), demotes both non-leader peers, applies 100 commands, takes leader.Snapshot(), promotes both peers back and applies ten more entries, reads the last configuration entry and emits a change_inputs CA_EVENT, then shuts down every instance. It restarts only the former leader over its own stores with the case flag, starts one fresh empty instance (own stores, its own MockFSM, connected to the leader in both directions), waits for the leader, records its reconstructed voter count, issues AddVoter for the fresh instance with prevIndex 0 and records the outcome, then rebuilds the two demoted peers with the flag disabled, reconnects them to the leader and waits. It emits a change_result CA_EVENT with the leader's reconstructed and replaced voter counts and server sets, the change outcome and error, whether the new member holds a vote and whether it was in the replaced configuration, the fresh instance's reconstructed voter count, and how many demoted peers adopted the rewritten configuration and how many of them ended with a vote.
experiment.responsibility: The leader computes a client membership change from configurations.latest and rebuilds its commitment from the resulting configuration, so whether a change commits with the replaced configuration's support is decided by that configuration rather than by the one recorded in the leader's log.

comparisons.description: Client-change case with the flag enabled: a node leading on a reconstructed configuration is not expected to commit a membership change that replaces the committed configuration with support that is not its majority.
Control: with the flag disabled the same node cannot be leader with the other members down, so no membership change commits.
Client-change case with the flag enabled: whether both peers that held votes in the replaced configuration ended up adopting the rewritten configuration in which they hold none.
Client-change case with the flag enabled: records that the member added by the change is not part of the configuration the change replaced.

experiment.revision_reason: Adds the client_change_on_reconstruction case with its flag-disabled control, in which a client membership change is issued to a node leading on a reconstructed configuration while the peers of the committed configuration are down, and those peers are then restarted to observe whether they adopt the rewritten configuration. Replaces the comparison set with the commit predicate, its control and the adoption and membership premises.
